title: Prime-power diagonal smooth orientation over a Noetherian base
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $p:P\to X$ be smooth, separated, of finite type and of pure relative dimension $r\geq0$ between Noetherian schemes with $\ell$ invertible [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume $p$ compactifiable [def-asd-compactifiable]. Use the ordinary small-etale derived categories and the compact-support right adjoint $p_n^!$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], with Tate twists [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. The diagonal first-Chern-class and deformation-to-the-normal-cone construction gives an orientation
$$\gamma_{p,n}:\Lambda_{n,P}(r)[2r]\xrightarrow{\sim}p_n^!\Lambda_{n,X}.$$
The inverse orientation is obtained from diagonal base change $p_n^!\Lambda_{n,X}\cong\Delta^*(p_1)_n^!\Lambda_{n,P}$, deformation of the diagonal section of $p_1:P\times_XP\to P$ to the zero section of $T_{P/X}$, and the zero-section restriction of inverse Kummer-normalized vector-bundle purity. Vector-bundle purity is normalized by integrating $c_1(\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}(1))$ to $1$, and by the ordered product on affine space. For every $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda_n)$, this orientation and the counit-defined exceptional tensor map give an isomorphism $p^*K(r)[2r]\xrightarrow{\sim}p_n^!K$.

These specified maps commute with Noetherian base change, open and etale restriction, and composition of smooth maps under exceptional transitivity. At relative dimension zero they are the etale adjunction comparisons. For $N\geq n$, coefficient reduction carries $\gamma_{p,N}$ to $\gamma_{p,n}$ under the counit-defined coefficient comparison; the comparison of Tate lines is induced by $u\mapsto u^{\ell^{N-n}}$. This assertion is on ordinary etale categories, without excellence or a ground-field hypothesis.

source.place: Theorem 7.19 and proof, and following paragraph on diagonal deformation and the Tate identification; finite prime-power ordinary-etale specialization. Uses the same general-Noetherian diagonal/DNC construction as the existing nodes thm-asd-smooth-tensor, prop-asd-smooth-base-change, lem-trf-finite-ring-section-deformation and thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity. Composition and coefficient normalization are the coordinate-tower and Kummer functoriality of that construction; this node states that extension explicitly rather than taking a trace-based construction.

proof.text: Put $A=\Lambda_n$ and $\omega_h=h_n^!A$. The self-product $W=P\times_XP$ is Noetherian, its first projection $p_1$ is separated finite type and smooth of dimension $r$, and its diagonal $\Delta$ is a regular closed immersion of codimension $r$ with normal bundle $T_{P/X}$. Indeed apply finite-type permanence, separated finite-type base change, smooth-dimension permanence and the diagonal regular-immersion lemma. A Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact by definition and quasi-separated by the locally-Noetherian lemma, so Nagata supplies compactifications for the separated finite-type maps used below. In particular the section-deformation lemma applies to $(p_1,\Delta)$; it supplies Noetherianity, smoothness and compactifiability of the deformation and normal-bundle maps. The same verifications apply after any Noetherian change of base.

source.place: Geometry of the diagonal and the ordinary Noetherian extension of the finite-stage argument

proof.text: Fix the normalization for affine space over a Noetherian base $S$. For $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, the ordinary finite projective-line adjunction has $G_qK=q^*K(1)[2]$ and counit $(1\otimes t_q)\mathrm{PF}^{-1}$, with $t_qc_1(\mathcal O(1))=1$. Its unit is the supported-diagonal formula of [det-sp-p1-adjunction]; the Noetherian diagonal integrals in [lem-amb-p1-diagonal-integrals] are its triangle identities. All coordinate-tower bases are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since they are finite type over S. No arbitrary-base integral theorem is needed. Compose this adjunction with open extension for $\mathbf A^1_S\subset\mathbf P^1_S$, and then successively in the ordered coordinate tower. This is precisely the affine-space adjunction and trace of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], with identity adjunction when $r=0$. Thus the chosen affine comparison $\Gamma_{r}:A(r)[2r]\to\omega_{p_r}$ uses the supported first Chern class of the diagonal and the prescribed integration normalization.

source.place: Affine-line diagonal class, projective-line integration and ordered products

proof.text:
Apply [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] to the self-base-change square of $p$. Its unit-coefficient comparison $p_2^*\omega_p\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p_1}$ restricts along $\Delta$ to $a_p:\omega_p\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta^*\omega_{p_1}$, because $p_2\Delta=1_P$. The normalized finite-ring section deformation gives $\delta_p:\Delta^*\omega_{p_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}z^*\omega_\pi$, where $\pi:T_{P/X}\to P$ and $z$ is zero. The same $\delta_p$ is the normalized comparison $\delta_{p_1,\Delta}$ of [lem-pur-noetherian-etale-section-specialization]: that lemma applies to $(p_1,\Delta)$ with $A=\Lambda_n$ (its regularity, smoothness and compactifiability hypotheses are those verified in Step 1), it uses the same Rees family $D=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_W\mathcal O_W[t,\mathcal I/t]$ and the same exceptional base-change fibre identifications, and both lemmas characterize $\kappa$ as the unique isomorphism $F\to a^*C$ restricting to $1_C$ at $t=1$. Hence the deformation factor of Step 12 and the comparison $\kappa$ of Step 16 are the ones used here. In [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] take the coefficient extension $F=\mathbf Q_\ell$, uniformizer $\ell$, and stage $n$; its coefficient ring is $A$. Denote its unit comparison by $v_\pi:A(r)[2r]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_\pi$. Set
$$\alpha_p=z^*(v_\pi^{-1})\circ\delta_p\circ a_p,\qquad\gamma_{p,n}=\alpha_p^{-1}.$$
The Tate comparison is exactly the ordinary roots-of-unity comparison in that theorem and [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. This proves the specified three-factor orientation is an isomorphism.

source.place: The displayed diagonal / deformation / inverse vector-bundle chain

proof.text:
For every $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, define
$$\gamma_{p,K}=\phi_{p,K}\circ(1\otimes\alpha_p^{-1}):p^*K(r)[2r]\longrightarrow p_n^!K,$$
with the tensor/shift unit identifications understood. Here $\phi_{p,K}$ is exactly the transpose of inverse compact-support projection followed by the unit-object counit, as specified in [thm-asd-smooth-tensor]. That theorem makes this actual map invertible for every ordinary derived input. Step 3 makes its other factor invertible. Therefore $\gamma_{p,K}$ is an isomorphism natural in $K$. This uses neither constructibility nor finite Tor amplitude of $K$.

source.place: Definition of gamma as the inverse orientation followed by the canonical tensor map

proof.text: We compute the orientation on an affine smooth chart $h:U\to V$, with a separated etale coordinate map $e:U\to\mathbf A^r_V$. Such charts exist by [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form]; their opens are Noetherian. On $U\times_VU$ the functions $e_j(u_2)-e_j(u_1)$ define an etale map to $\mathbf A^r_U$, by etale base change and the translation isomorphism. Its zero fibre is $U\times_{\mathbf A^r_V}U$, etale separated over $U$. The diagonal is a clopen section of that fibre; remove its complementary closed subscheme. This gives a neighbourhood of the diagonal whose inverse image of zero is exactly the diagonal. The section-deformation theorem identifies the normal frame with the classes of these coordinate differences and identifies its normalized $\delta$ with the identity on the standard section invariant.

source.place: Steps 1 and 2: Cartesian square of centres and induced normal frame

proof.text:
The self-base-change comparison $a_h$ computed using $(u_1,e(u_2))$ agrees with the one computed using $(u_1,e(u_2)-e(u_1))$. Indeed these charts differ by translation by the section $e(u_1)$, and [lem-trf-ambient-affine-translation-trace] states that this translation preserves the actual ordered trace. Taking mates identifies the dualizing comparisons. The vector-bundle orientation in the normal frame of Step 5 is the ordered affine orientation: the finite-ring section theorem states this normalization, and vector-bundle purity specifies its counit. The affine orientation is compatible with base change along $h$: for $h':\mathbf A^r_U\to\mathbf A^r_V$, the map $\beta_{p_r,h}:h'^*\omega_{p_r,V}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p_r,U}$ of [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] is the transpose of the pulled-back counit through compact-support base change, and the equality $t_{p_{r,U}}\circ C_{r,h}=h^*t_{p_{r,V}}$ of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] says exactly that this transpose carries $h'^*\Gamma_{r,V}$ to $\Gamma_{r,U}$. The chart $(u_1,e(u_2))$ is the base change of $e$ along $h$, so this identifies $a_h$, under $E_e$ and the etale comparison for that chart, with the restriction along the section $(u,e(u))$ of $\Gamma_{r,U}$; the translation by $e(u_1)$ moves this section to zero. Pasting the self-product squares through $h=p_re$, using etale adjoint locality and mate pasting, now gives
$$\alpha_h=e^*(\Gamma_r^{-1})\circ E_e,\quad E_e:\omega_h\xrightarrow{\sim}e^*\omega_{p_r}.$$
Here $E_e$ is the counit-preserving etale comparison. The tensor-mate identity for etale precomposition identifies $\gamma_{h,K}$ with that same coordinate adjunction for every $K$.

source.place: Steps 3 and 4: all three factors have the specified affine chart normalization

proof.text: For $b:X'\to X$ with $X'$ Noetherian, let $b':P'\to P$ and $B:b'^*\omega_p\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p'}$ be the canonical exceptional mate. The self-product square after base change is the pullback of the original square. Compact-support exchange is compatible with successive base changes and composition, and its exceptional mates obey pasting. These equations identify the pullback of $a_p$ with $a_{p'}$. The section-deformation theorem identifies the pullback of $\delta_p$ with $\delta_{p'}$, under these same fibre and normal-bundle comparisons. Thus the first two factors of $\alpha_p$ commute with this arbitrary Noetherian base change.

source.place: Base-change compatibility of the diagonal and deformation factors

proof.text:
For the vector factor, integration on each bundle trivialization is the affine trace. The equality $t_{p'_r}C_{r,b}=b^*t_{p_r}$ in the affine-space trace theorem therefore identifies the two integration maps on the pulled-back trivializing cover. Their compact-support source is concentrated in degree zero: locally it is isomorphic to $A[0]$ by that theorem. The definition of vector integration, full faithfulness of the degree-zero embedding and sheaf-Hom gluing give equality globally. Taking mates gives the corresponding equality for $v_\pi$ and its zero-section restriction. Together with Step 7 this proves
$$\alpha_{p'}B=b'^*\alpha_p.$$
The tensor/base-change identity in [prop-asd-smooth-base-change], with $\alpha_{p'}^{-1}=B(b'^*\alpha_p)^{-1}$ substituted, gives $\beta_{p,b,K}b'^*\gamma_{p,K}=\gamma_{p',b^*K}$, with the canonical twist comparison.

source.place: Base-change compatibility of vector integration and the tensor composite

proof.text: Open or separated etale restriction on the source preserves the specified orientation. First let $V\subset X$ be open and $U\subset P_V=P\times_XV$ open, with $h=p|_U$. Restriction of the base to $V$ is the Noetherian base change of Steps 7 and 8. For the open $U\subset P_V$ the three factors restrict separately. (a) $U\times_VU$ is open in $P_V\times_VP_V$; the maps $\beta$ of [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] for the two self-squares are transposes of pulled-back counits, so the etale comparisons of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] and mate pasting carry the restriction of $a_{p_V}$ to $a_h$. (b) The normalized comparison commutes with the Noetherian base change $U\to P_V$ of the section base and with the open neighbourhood $U\times_VU$ of the diagonal, whose square of centres is Cartesian, by [lem-trf-finite-ring-section-deformation]. (c) $T_{U/V}=T_{P_V/V}|_U$, and by [def-amb-vector-integration] both integrations are the unique maps restricting to the affine traces on trivializations, so $v_\pi$ restricts to $v_{\pi_U}$. Thus $\alpha_p|_U$ corresponds to $\alpha_h$ under the counit-preserving open comparison; in particular Steps 5 and 6 compute $\alpha_p$ itself on every coordinate chart. For a separated etale $j:P'\to P$, compute both orientations on a further smooth coordinate cover using Steps 5 and 6: both are the pullback of the same ordered affine orientation under the counit-preserving etale comparison. Successive etale charts compose, and their exceptional comparisons compose by mate pasting. The two unit-object maps are between equally shifted locally free rank-one sheaves by smooth tensor, so full faithfulness and sheaf-Hom gluing promote this coverwise equality to equality globally. The etale-precomposition tensor identity then gives the equality for every $K$. Base restrictions are already covered by Steps 7 and 8.

source.place: Etale source restriction and gluing of orientation maps

proof.text:
Let $P\xrightarrow p X\xrightarrow q Y$ be smooth of dimensions $r,s$. Let $c:(qp)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}p^!q^!$ be the counit-preserving comparison. Put $u_{p,q}=c^{-1}\phi_{p,\omega_q}:p^*\omega_q\otimes\omega_p\to\omega_{qp}$. Transpose under $R(qp)_!\dashv(qp)^!$. The projection-composition identity of [lem-amb-shriek-tensor-composition], and the composite counit $\epsilon_q\circ Rq_!\epsilon_p$, identify the transpose of
$$c^{-1}p^!(\phi_{q,K})\phi_{p,q^*K\otimes\omega_q}$$
with the transpose of $\phi_{qp,K}(1\otimes u_{p,q})$. Both are inverse projection for $p$, its unit-object counit, inverse projection for $q$, and its counit, in that order. The adjunction bijection gives equality. Thus composition for all $\gamma_{p,K}$ reduces to
$$\alpha_{qp}^{-1}=u_{p,q}(p^*\alpha_q^{-1}\otimes\alpha_p^{-1}),$$
All twists are reassociated canonically.

source.place: Formal projection/counit part of smooth composition

proof.text: Choose compatible affine charts $U\to\mathbf A^r_V$ for $p$ and $V\to\mathbf A^s_T$ for $q$. The composite chart $U\to\mathbf A^{r+s}_T$ is etale, by base change and composition of etale maps. Order the $r$ fibre coordinates before the $s$ base coordinates. Step 6 identifies the diagonal orientations with the counit-preserving chart adjunction comparisons. The $(r+s)$ coordinate adjunction and the successive $r$ and $s$ adjunctions have the same Hom bijection: the same ordered succession of affine-line Hom bijections, with the same etale Hom bijections. Therefore their counits are equal. Coherent compact-support composition and mate pasting identify their right-adjoint comparisons; uniqueness of the counit-preserving comparison proves the unit equality in Step 10 on these charts. Both sides are maps between equal shifts of rank-one locally constant sheaves, so full faithfulness and sheaf gluing give the equality globally. Step 10 proves composition for every $K$. The shifts $2r,2s$ are even, so no sign is introduced.

source.place: Coordinate-tower argument for composition; orientation equality checked as a sheaf map

proof.text: When $r=0$, smoothness is etaleness. Apply [lem-pur-finite-smooth-gamma-normalization] at the given stage $n$. Its three-factor orientation is exactly Step 3 and its tensor composite is Step 4. It says that the orientation becomes the identity under the etale sum-adjunction identification, and that the tensor composite is the unique right-adjoint comparison preserving the sum/evaluation counit. Thus the claimed dimension-zero normalization holds, including identity maps, open immersions, nontrivial etale covers and the empty scheme.

source.place: Etale normalization of the same three-factor map

proof.text:
For coefficient reduction write $A=\Lambda_N$, $B=\Lambda_n$ and $S_T=(-)\otimes_A^LB$. Use the canonical compactification coefficient map $b:S_YRp_{!,A}\to Rp_{!,B}S_P$ in [lem-pur-exceptional-coefficient-comparison], at the bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs used here. Its quotient cocycle is checked with a common compactification: the proper comparison is the mate of the scalar/pullback associator, hence consecutive proper comparisons agree by mate pasting; the open comparison is the balancing identity $(m\otimes b)\otimes c=m\otimes bc$ on the open and zero off it. Pasting gives the cocycle for $b$. Hence the cited coefficient lemma defines $c_K:S_Pp_A^!K\to p_B^!S_XK$ by
$$\epsilon_B\,Rp_{!,B}(c_K)=S_X\epsilon_A\,b_{p_A^!K}^{-1}.$$
We use only $K=A_X$ and the unit objects for the diagonal projection, vector bundle and deformation. These are bounded constructible finite-Tor; their dualizing objects are shifted locally free rank-one sheaves by smooth tensor. The coefficient lemma supplies the tensor and geometric-base-change identities for these actual $c$, without assuming $c$ invertible.

source.place: Counit-defined coefficient map and quotient cocycle

proof.text: At the affine line, compare the Kummer sequences with exponents $\ell^N$ and $\ell^n$. The vertical map on their first $\mathbf G_m$ is $u\mapsto u^{\ell^{N-n}}$ and on their last $\mathbf G_m$ is the identity; their squares commute since $(u^{\ell^{N-n}})^{\ell^n}=u^{\ell^N}$. The kernel map is therefore the power map on roots of unity, and the connecting morphism sends the $N$-level first Chern class to the $n$-level class. The ordinary supported Kummer class is defined by this boundary and derived scalar extension, so the same assertion holds with diagonal support. The Tate lemma identifies $S_TA_T(1)$ with $B_T(1)$ by precisely this power map. Tensor powers give all twists used here. This is a comparison of the Kummer maps themselves; no tensoring-cohomology assertion with a nonflat quotient is used.

source.place: Kummer normalization at consecutive exponents; Stacks 03PL, etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-kummer-sequence

proof.text:
For the projective line let $b_{q,R}:R(1)[2]\oplus R\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*R(1)[2]$ be its two-summand decomposition, $R=A,B$. Under the proper coefficient comparison, its first summand reduces to the shifted twisted unit (transpose the identity), and Step 14 identifies its second summand with $c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ over $B$. Thus $S(b_{q,A})$ becomes $b_{q,B}$. Taking inverse and the second projection shows that $t_{q,A}$ becomes $t_{q,B}$. The canonical proper coefficient map is the projection map after restriction of scalars, by [lem-pur-etale-scalar-mate-projection]; it is invertible on these inputs by the proper projection theorem. Open extension and the ordered affine-line tower preserve this counit identity, by mate pasting. Consequently the affine-space right-adjoint comparison at $A$ reduces to the corresponding $B$ comparison. On vector-bundle trivializations this proves
$$z^*(v_{\pi,B}^{-1})\,z^*c_{\pi,A}=S(z^*v_{\pi,A}^{-1}).$$
Both sides are maps between equally shifted rank-one $B$-sheaves. Full faithfulness and sheaf gluing give this equality globally. The needed projection/coefficient compatibility is the ringed exchange/tensor identity applied to the coefficient-change square.

source.place: Coefficient compatibility of the normalized projective-line splitting, ordered counit and vector factor

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-diagonal-orientation-compatibility] to $(p_1,\Delta)$, with its normalized deformation family $F_A,F_B$ and section lines $C_A,C_B$. Take $e_F$ and $e_C$ to be section pullbacks of the counit-defined coefficient comparisons of Step 13. Their restrictions at $t=1$ agree: this is the geometric-base-change identity for $c$ in that lemma, applied to the deformation fibre $i_1$. The orientation-compatibility lemma gives
$$\delta_Be_C=e_0S(\delta_A).$$
It does not require any of these coefficient maps to be invertible. The same geometric-base-change identity on the diagonal self-square gives $a_{p,B}c_{p,A}=(\Delta^*c_{p_1,A})S(a_{p,A})$. Compose this with the displayed deformation equality and the vector equality of Step 15. All middle comparison maps cancel by substitution, yielding
$$\alpha_{p,B}c_{p,A}=S(\alpha_{p,A}).$$
Multiplying by $S(\alpha_{p,A}^{-1})$ gives $c_{p,A}S(\gamma_{p,N})=\gamma_{p,n}$. In particular the coefficient comparison on this unit dualizing object is an isomorphism, as a consequence of this equality. This is the requested reduction of the specified orientation, with the power-map Tate identification of Step 14.

source.place: Normalized deformation and diagonal factors under coefficient reduction
